chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from one of his companions, from Abu al-Abbas al-Baqbaaq, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Leaving off the sin is easier than seeking repentance, and how many momentary lusts have inherited prolonged grief; and death exposes the world, so it does not leave the one of understanding with any joy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of preventing sin rather than just repenting for it?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to Imam Ali (AS), underscores the strategic wisdom of preventative piety (zuhd) over reactive repentance, a core theme in Shia ethical theology. It highlights the transient nature of worldly pleasures by noting that death exposes their vanity, leaving no enduring joy for the discerning mind. This teaching aligns with the Shia emphasis on 'guarding against sin' as a higher station than merely seeking forgiveness after the fact.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from one of his companions, from Abu Al Abbas Al Baqbaaq who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Neglecting the sins is easier than seeking the Forgiveness, and how may lustful desires of a moment inherit the prolonged grief; and the death exposes the world so it does not leave the one with understanding, any happiness’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from certain individuals of his people from al- ‘Abbas al- Baqbaq who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, “Avoiding sin is easier than pleading for forgiveness. How many are the cases of very short period of lustful activities that cause prolonged sadness. Death disgraces the world (uncovers its worthlessness) and it has not left any happiness for the people of proper understanding.’”
